title: Afia Efere
author: Iquo Bassey
desc: The ceremonial Efik white soup, made without palm oil at all — a whole chicken, four cups of water, and pounded yam dissolved into it as the thickener.
longDesc: Afia efere is the soup Efik ceremonies are not complete without, and the author's own occasion for learning it was her father's coronation. It is made without palm oil, which is what distinguishes the ceremonial version from the everyday one and what keeps it white. A whole chicken is marinated thirty minutes, steamed until the water evaporates and then twenty minutes more, and four cups of water go in with the crayfish, pepper, iwun and Aidan fruit. The thickener is a medium slice of yam, boiled and pounded very firm with no water, flattened and dissolved into the soup.
ingredients: 1 whole broiler chicken, cut into pieces
A handful of smoked fish, shredded
2 pieces Aidan fruit, the size of a little finger
// The thickener, which is not in the original ingredient list
1 medium slice of yam, boiled and pounded
steps: Season the chicken and marinate 30 minutes.
Boil the yam separately and pound it until very firm, adding no water at all.
Steam the chicken until the water evaporates, then cook 20 minutes more, until half cooked.
Add the 4 cups of water, the ground crayfish, the shredded smoked fish, the dried pepper, the blended iwun, the Aidan fruit and the seasoning, and bring to the boil.
Flatten the pounded yam into 3 or 4 pieces and add them to the soup.
Boil until the yam has dissolved completely.
Add the okro if using and cook 5 minutes.
Taste, adjust the salt, and serve.
chefTips: No palm oil. That is what makes it the ceremonial version and what keeps the soup pale.
Pound the yam with no water added. Firm and dry is what you want — wet pounded yam will not dissolve cleanly, it will go slimy.
Flatten it into three or four pieces before it goes in. Flat pieces dissolve from both sides.
Steam the chicken until the water evaporates first, then twenty minutes more. The dry-steaming concentrates the flavour before any water goes in.
Iwun is African nutmeg, two pieces blended, and the Aidan fruit pieces should be the size of a little finger. Those two are the aromatics that make afia efere taste of itself.
Okro is optional and goes in last for five minutes. With it the soup draws slightly; without, it stays clean.
The yam is not in the printed ingredient list — it comes from a clarification in the comments. It is the thickener of a thickened soup, so it is listed above under its own heading.
commonMistakes: Adding water while pounding the yam.
Dropping the pounded yam in as a single ball.
Adding the four cups of water before the chicken has dry-steamed.
Over-cooking the okro until it goes stringy.
sources: Adapted from 'How to make Afia Efere Recipe – White Soup', byline '1Qfoodplatter'. Quantities as printed: whole broiler chicken cut into pieces — NO WEIGHT GIVEN; handful smoked fish shredded; 6 fingers okro (optional); 2 tablespoons ground crayfish; 1 tablespoon dried pepper; 2 pieces blended African nutmeg (iwun); 2 pieces Aidan fruit (size of little finger); 1 crayfish seasoning tablet; 1 beef seasoning cube; salt. Plus 4 cups water from the method. Yield not specified.

PROVENANCE, and it is excellent: the headnote states 'Traditional Efik events are not complete without Afia Efere', and the author's inspiration was her father's coronation ceremony. The soup is prepared WITHOUT palm oil, which is what distinguishes the ceremonial version from the daily one.

INGREDIENT-LIST DISCREPANCY, flagged: the YAM — the thickener of a thickened soup — is NOT in the printed ingredient list. It comes from a clarification in the page's comments, given as 'a medium slice', boiled and pounded until resilient, flattened into 3 or 4 pieces and added to dissolve completely. It is listed above under a clear heading rather than inserted silently.

Method and times as printed: marinate the seasoned chicken 30 minutes; boil the yam separately and 'pound until very firm (no water added)'; steam the chicken until the water evaporates, then '20 minutes more until half-cooked'; add 4 cups water, crayfish, fish, pepper, spices and seasoning and boil; add the flattened pounded yam and 'boil until completely dissolved'; okro 5 minutes.

ON THE THICKENER: this is the third source in this collection for the white-soup family, and like the two Igbo nsala recipes it uses YAM and not ofor (NGA048, NGA049). Three sources, all yam, none using ofor.

ON THE SOURCE: a prior research pass concluded that editan, iwuk edesi, usung, ndek uyo, ukang and fisherman's soup were 'simply absent from the named-author record'. Four of the six turned out to be documented, all on this one site, which had been under-searched rather than exhausted. Usung and ndek uyo do appear to be genuinely absent — no named-author source surfaced for either on any query.
storage: 3 days refrigerated. The yam thickening tightens when cold.
reheating: Low heat with a little water.
healthBenefits: No palm oil, so much lower in fat than most Nigerian soups.
Chicken and smoked fish give lean protein.
African nutmeg and Aidan fruit are traditionally used as digestives.
Low in carbohydrate for a thickened soup.
culturalNote: Afia efere is ceremonial food and the absence of palm oil is the marker of that — the everyday version is made with it, the version for a coronation or a traditional rite is not. It is the Efik member of a family that includes Igbo ofe nsala, and across the whole family the pattern holds: no palm oil, yam as the thickener, and a trio of aromatic dried spices doing the work that oil and pepper do elsewhere.
